_schema_help.template_vs_project: screen-normalization.example.json is the reusable starter example with placeholders. Copy its structure to screen-normalization.json for a project, replace the examples with real parity-map rows, and keep the example file unchanged. screen-normalization.json is the governed Stage 6 project record consumed by audit:prototype and pinned by screen-manifest.json.
_schema_help.purpose: This is the row-to-visual-plan bridge. It says where every applicable legacy_user_flows.xlsx row will appear: as a screen, a state or interaction on a screen, navigation, or a non-visual behavior.
_schema_help.direction: Behavior -> screen: What needs to be represented? Start with each governed parity-map row and decide its visual destination or explicit non-visual disposition.
_schema_help.relationship_to_manifest: This plan is written before drawing. screen-manifest.json is written after drawing, references this file in normalization, and stores its evidence hash in normalization_sha256. Matching screen ids and surface_key values connect the planned placement to the exported screen.

fields.rows: All applicable parity-map rows, each classified exactly once.
fields.rows[].row: The physical row number in analysis/legacy_user_flows.xlsx. It is the stable link back to the legacy behavior.
fields.rows[].classification: One of surface, state, action, overlay, navigation or non-visual. See classification_values below.
fields.rows[].screen: Stable screen id planned here and later used unchanged in screen-manifest.json. Required for every visual classification; omitted for non-visual.
fields.rows[].surface_key: Canonical identity of the screen: channel + route family + primary user task + stable layout. It must match that screen's surface_key in screen-manifest.json.
fields.rows[].element: The exact state, action, overlay or navigation label on the named screen. Required for those four classifications, forbidden for surface and non-visual.
fields.rows[].note: Short evidence-based reason for this classification and placement; explain why this is or is not a separate screen.
fields.excluded_rows: Rows deliberately removed from migration scope by an explicit Stage 4 do-not-port decision. Exclusion is not a seventh classification.
fields.excluded_rows[].row: The physical parity-map row excluded from the target.
fields.excluded_rows[].finding: Identifier of the Stage 4 finding or owner decision authorizing the exclusion.
fields.excluded_rows[].reason: Human-readable summary of why the behavior will not be ported.
fields._notes: File-level provenance and maintenance notes for this particular record. They explain how it was produced; they are not row classifications.
fields._schema_help: Embedded documentation only. Audits accept it but do not treat it as migration evidence.

classification_values.surface: A distinct visual destination with its own purpose, structure or route. It needs screen and surface_key, but no element.
classification_values.state: A condition of an existing screen, such as empty, loading, validation error or permission denied. element names that state.
classification_values.action: A user operation performed on an existing screen, such as Save or Delete. element names the action or control.
classification_values.overlay: A dialog, drawer, popover or menu displayed over an existing screen. element names the overlay.
classification_values.navigation: A transition that starts on the named screen and leads elsewhere. element names the navigation step.
classification_values.non-visual: Backend, integration, scheduled or enforcement behavior with no distinct visual representation. It has no screen, surface_key or element.

_schema_help.example_reading: A row with classification=state, screen=sign-in, surface_key='web + /login + sign in + centred card' and element='authentication failed' means: this legacy behavior is represented by the authentication-failed state of the sign-in screen, not by a separate wireframe.

_notes: Stage 6 draft by UX Designer assignment UX-006-01, generated 2026-10-02T20:35:50Z (UTC from code) from analysis/legacy_user_flows.xlsx, sheet "User Flows" (read-only, 210 business rows of UF-001..UF-018), column J Stage 4 destination notes, and analysis/stages/stage-04/stage-04-requirements-revision.md D-001..D-025. Not reviewed and not approved.

Accounting of all 210 business rows, each exactly once: 145 classified in rows[] (keep or change: surface 25, navigation 8, non-visual 29, state 47, action 25, overlay 11), 34 in excluded_rows[] (Stage 4 do-not-port), 31 in deferred_rows[] (Stage 4 defer), 0 pending (UX-006-09 placements; rows 24 and 26 reclassified from non-visual to state in UX-006-13).

Deferred rows (UX-006-10, 2026-10-03T14:11:12Z UTC from code): the 31 Stage 4 defer rows are recorded in deferred_rows (decision D-NNN from column J, reason, resume_condition = the column J responsibility and condition), accepted by prototype-audit.js since PR #48. They are not classified, not excluded and not drawn; they return to Stage 6 with their slice. Earlier versions of this record listed them in this note because the schema had no field (backlog item 12).

Placements (UX-006-09, 2026-10-03T13:53:51Z UTC from code; UX choice of place within existing screens, owner direction relayed by Codex; checked at Stage 7, shown to the owner at Stage 8): row 161 re-estimate -> time-editor action; row 174 delete note confirmation -> note-editor overlay; row 189 safe markup display -> non-visual rendering rule; row 208 export menu -> project-page navigation (Export link); row 212 story/task PDF -> story-page action (Export link). No keep or change row is pending any more.

The normalization is general. Screen ids and surface keys are planning identities; route families are labels, not implementation URLs. Current drawing status (UX-006-14, 2026-10-05T11:45:37Z UTC from code): all 25 screens have real exports listed in screen-manifest.json, which is the pinned record of the drawn files, their roles and states, and the open visual remainders; every row that Stage 7 pass 001 found without a drawn destination is drawn. Stage 7 pass 002 findings F-001..F-006 are being corrected in Stage 6. Element names may be refined when they are drawn.

Role variations (viewer, editor and admin per project; system administrator) follow the map (rows 23-26, 33, 34, 41, 42, 55, 76, 82, 91) and the SDD permission matrix (D-001, no extension of rights by default); no screen encodes a role ladder. UX-006-13 (Stage 7 pass 001 F-001/F-002): role views are drawn where the composition changes: iteration-page viewer (iteration-viewer-desktop), editor (iteration-export-menu-desktop, no Delete iteration) and admin (list-desktop, Delete iteration); task-page viewer (task-viewer-desktop); projects-list for the system administrator (projects-list-desktop: Create project, System information link). The Hidden column of the projects list and the Hidden checkbox of the project editor follow the hide permission (rows 76, 81) as separate permission-conditioned states (present: projects-list-desktop, projects-list-hide-desktop, project-editor-desktop; absent: projects-list-member-desktop); which roles hold hide is deferred to the SDD matrix (D-001, D-011) (UX-006-14, candidate correction for Stage 7 pass 002 F-002). Also drawn: projects-list without Create project and System information (projects-list-member-desktop), project-page admin with the export menu (project-page-admin-desktop), story-page viewer with the export menu (story-viewer-export-desktop), person-page viewer (person-page-viewer-desktop) and person-editor project admin (person-editor-admin-desktop). Role variations with an otherwise unchanged composition are recorded as states, not drawn separately: people-list without Create person for viewers and editors; project-page without Edit, Create iteration and Add note for viewers.

Navigation model (UX-006-06, 2026-10-03T11:21:52Z UTC from code; Starter guidance "Navigation And Identity Before Drawing"): journeys come from the map. Sign-in (row 8) goes to the requested permitted page (row 10), else to the current iteration when exactly one project is accessible (row 18), else to the projects list. From there: project (83), iteration with local tabs Stories / Tasks / Statistics / Accuracy / Board (92, 106, 109, 113, 114), story (127), task (143), then the task editor (134) or time editor (149). People: people list (37), person page (40; "me" row 188 opens the same page for the signed-in person), person editor (43), timesheet (162). Aggregate timesheet (165) from the projects list; search (178), history (186), error (56) and system information (55, system administrators only). Hierarchical pages show the breadcrumb Top / Project / Iteration / Story / Task (row 185) with a plain current item and no breadcrumb at the root. Editors return to the originating page as rows 43, 78, 88, 121, 134 and 149 state, on same-application paths only (D-004); carrying list position in the URL is a proposal for the owner, not a requirement. Roles: one interface; actions are absent without permission (row 26); the matrix is set at SDD (D-001).

Identity (UX-006-06, revised UX-006-07 by owner direction relayed by Codex): no map row names a photo or avatar. The person and "me" pages (rows 40, 188) show an initials avatar from the stored initials (rows 37, 43, 44) as the identity and fallback (Stage 6 draft). A profile photo is an explicitly unapproved extension that does not block representing the existing profile; no upload and no identity integration.

Editor actions (rows 81, 90, 125 and 139 record Update/Reset; owner direction UX-006-07, relayed by Codex): editors offer Save, Reset and Cancel. Save stores and returns to the origin; Reset restores the initial values and stays on the form; Cancel leaves without saving and returns to the origin. Neither replaces the other. Row mappings are unchanged.

App-shell (UX-006-09): no standalone app-shell surface remains. The shared top bar and breadcrumb are drawn inside every export; rows 19 (sign out), 185 (breadcrumb), 188 (me) and 192 (print view) are recorded on projects-list, task-page, person-page and iteration-page respectively. Only the print view needs an export of its own.
